description: A real Chrome on a headless Wayland display on this host. The owner watches and drives its window live in a Report `window` block; agents read and drive the same window with these tools.

exposes_tools.name: window_ls
exposes_tools.description: The open windows of the desktop and its apps. `windows` lists each open window as `{window_id, app, title, width, height}` (`app` is null for a window no app launched); `window_id` names one window until it closes and is never reused. `apps` lists each app as `{app, running, src}`: `src` is the path a Report `window` block shows that app's main window from (its most recent open window), so add `{ "kind": "window", "payload": { "src": <src> } }` to a Report to let the owner watch and use it. Showing a block, or `page_open`, starts an app that is not running.

exposes_tools.name: window_cat
exposes_tools.description: A PNG screenshot of one open window, taken after the window has had a moment (under a second) to draw, plus `{window_id, title, width, height}`. An effect that takes longer (a page still loading, an animation) needs another call. A closed window is an error (-32404), never an old image. Coordinates for `window_input` are pixels of this image.

exposes_tools.name: window_input
exposes_tools.description: Sends pointer and keyboard input to one open window, in order, as the one seat the owner also uses (the last input wins). Coordinates are window pixels, as in `window_cat`. Events: `{type:"click", x, y, button?}` (`left` by default, `middle`, `right`); `{type:"move", x, y}`; `{type:"scroll", x, y, dx, dy}` (pixels, positive is right and down); `{type:"key", keys}`, one key or chord on a US layout such as `"enter"`, `"ctrl+l"`, `"shift+tab"` or `"pagedown"`; `{type:"text", text}`, printable US-ASCII plus newline and tab only (no IME: use `page_open` for a URL). Returns `{ok: true}`; read the result back with `window_cat`.

x.description: click, move, scroll: window pixels from the left.

y.description: click, move, scroll: window pixels from the top.

button.description: click: the mouse button, `left` when absent.

dx.description: scroll: pixels to the right (negative: left).

keys.description: key: one key, or modifiers and a key joined by `+` (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`).

text.description: text: printable US-ASCII, newline and tab; at most 1000 characters.

exposes_tools.name: page_open
exposes_tools.description: Opens an http or https URL in Chrome's visible tab, the one the owner also sees, replacing what it showed; starts Chrome when it is not running. Returns `{url, title, loaded}` after the page's load event; `loaded: false` when the page committed but its load event had not come within 20 s (it may still go on). A navigation that gets no answer within 20 s at all is an error (-32503), and so is a page that failed to load. Refused (-32409), naming the pages, when no tab or more than one tab may be visible (a second window, a popup, a dialog). The title and url are cut at 1000 and 4096 characters.

url.description: An absolute http:// or https:// URL.

exposes_tools.name: page_cat
exposes_tools.description: The visible Chrome tab's `{url, title, text, text_truncated}`: `text` is the page's rendered text, cut at 100000 characters (`text_truncated` says whether it was); the title and url are cut at 1000 and 4096. Refused, naming the pages, when no tab or more than one tab may be visible (a second window, a popup, a dialog), and when Chrome is not running (-32503); it does not start Chrome.

chrome_binary.description: Absolute path of the Chrome executable: Google Chrome stable unpacked with `dpkg -x`, or Chrome for Testing (see the plugin README). The plugin does not bundle Chrome.

bwrap_binary.description: Absolute path of bubblewrap (`bwrap`). Chrome always runs inside a bwrap sandbox that shows it only its profile, its own home, the Chrome install, system libraries and fonts; without a working bwrap the plugin does not start and Chrome never runs.

width.description: Window width in pixels (320 to 3840). Every window is maximized to this size.

max_fps.description: Frame rate cap of a watched window (1 to 60). An unwatched window draws once a second.

proxy_server.description: Optional proxy for every Chrome request, `<scheme>://<host>:<port>` with scheme http, https, socks4 or socks5 (no user name or password), passed as Chrome's --proxy-server. Chrome does not inherit the service's proxy environment. Unset: Chrome connects directly.
